02 · Mining · Democratic Republic of Congo

Mining the heart of Africa's mineral belt

Okapilands SARL operates Direct Shipping Ore across multiple concessions in the DRC Copperbelt, pairing field geology with geobotanical prospecting and an engineering practice recognised by the Institute of Materials, Minerals and Mining.

3+Active concessions
Cu · CoPrimary deposits
W · LiStrategic minerals
DSODirect shipping model

Direct Shipping Ore

Our Direct Shipping Ore (DSO) approach provides immediate cash flow by selling high grade, surface level copper cobalt oxide material to local warehouses. This strategy funds our ongoing exploration without equity dilution, creating a self sustaining operational model that accelerates our path to discovery while demonstrating early economic viability.

Material is processed in the DRC or Zambia and offered on FOB or CIF terms.

03 · Materials and Innovation

Building with what the land discards

We use waste from agriculture and turn it into construction materials. Rice husk and bamboo leaves become an alkaline activated binder that absorbs CO₂ as it cures, replacing cement in the walls we raise.

UNEP · COP30 · Belém

Featured in the UN Environment Programme Catalogue of Climate Solutions for Buildings

Presented at COP30 in Belém, the catalogue gathers more than 90 cases from over 40 countries across the full building lifecycle. Okapiland appears on page 47: From Mining Waste to Building Blocks in the DRC.

32Rammed earth villas, Nsele Ecological City
6Hospitals under construction
Schoolsand public places
367Workers trained in low carbon construction

Hospitals built from the waste stream

Structural walls use stabilised rammed earth and compressed earth blocks, reinforced with a geopolymer binder made from rice husk, bamboo and local clay rather than cement. Metakaolin produced on site from native kaolin adds strength, while green roofs and perlite insulation deliver passive cooling for patients and equipment.

Nsele Ecological City integrates 32 rammed earth villas with swale and Permavoid drainage, green roofing, an air purification bioreactor, 250 kVA of biogas power and treated borehole water.

High performance material innovation

Bio grapheneDerived from lignin and agricultural residue, with flash graphene from bagasse and sugar waste for supercapacitors and electronics, and bio graphite for lithium batteries.
Bio cokeThe world's first negative carbon bio coke for steel furnaces, developed with the largest EU automobile company as a selected finalist at TRL 6.
Black Zero biocharEngineered pyrolysis turns biomass into biochar that replaces cement and bitumen and keeps removing CO₂ throughout its life.
Thermal backfillWith Porcement and the high voltage cable industry, a four season backfill made entirely from UK waste, reaching 6.2 W/mK over a 40 year design life.

04 · Agriminerals

Minerals that restore soil, water and air

Our patented Agriminerals technology turns farm waste and water purification residuals into active mineral products, closing the loop so that every litre of water we clean generates resources for growing and building.

I

High grade composting mineral

Advanced composting chemistry converts around 20 tonnes of organic waste every month into high grade compost and a mineral soil conditioner.

II

Carbon capture

Biochar and algae systems lock carbon away permanently. Spirulina cultivation alone has captured 2,000 kg of CO₂ alongside food production.

III

Bioremediation

Three hundred 50 kg mycelium colonisation bags and 2,500 activated bamboo stakes treat mining tailings through engineered strata of geopolymer, rust membrane and activated carbon.

IV

Water purification

Seven cartridge types built from agricultural geopolymer, activated carbon, flash graphene, rammed earth and seashell lime purify water from Kinshasa to Lusaka and Zimbabwe.

70,000+People served with clean water
20,000Residents of Nsele supplied
3,500Cartridges distributed free
365Community trainers certified
05 · Smart Farming

From waste to feast

At Shelthorpe Garden in Loughborough, with The African Oasis CIC and OmniGro, an abandoned allotment became a sensor guided urban farm. The same model now feeds families from Loughborough to Kinshasa and Harare.

British Science Festival · Guildhall Square

Named the star of the programme

Invited to the British Science Festival with two dedicated locations, our drop in activity From Waste to Feast asked a simple question: how could today's waste become tomorrow's dinner? Visitors built hot compost, met carbon capturing algae and planted mushrooms of their own.

Our research unit works alongside the Royal Horticultural Society and British Science Week, turning the garden into a living laboratory.

Intelligent growing

OmniGro smart containers monitor root zone temperature, nutrient concentration, dissolved oxygen, pH and light in real time and stream the data to a central dashboard. Produce travels to food banks and schools while still growing, arriving fresher than any supermarket shelf.

LED vertical systems grow microgreens and aquatic plants selected for carbon capture per unit of biomass.
